strings.web.nav.label: Dashboard navigation
strings.web.announce.label: Status updates from BedrockRelay
strings.web.home.tagline: Bring Minecraft chat into Discord, choose your channels, and install the pack from one place.
strings.web.home.step1Text: Pick a Discord server you manage and approve BedrockRelay.
strings.web.home.step2Text: Over SFTP in one click, or download it. No token to copy.
strings.web.home.step3Text: As soon as your Minecraft server connects, pick where chat goes.
strings.web.guild.subtitle: Manage this Discord server's Minecraft relay.
strings.web.guild.subtitleConnected: The Minecraft servers connected to this Discord server, and their channels.
strings.web.guild.chooseText: You need a Discord server with Manage Server permission to continue.
strings.web.guild.noServers: No Minecraft servers registered here yet.
strings.web.proximity.title: Proximity voice
strings.web.proximity.intro: Linked players opt in by joining the selected lobby. BedrockRelay then moves nearby players into temporary voice rooms.
strings.web.proximity.noServers: Set up a Minecraft server of your own before enabling proximity voice.
strings.web.proximity.lobbyHelp: The lobby must be silent: turn off Speak for the everyone role in it. Leaving the lobby and its BedrockRelay rooms opts a player out.
strings.web.proximity.permissions: The bot needs View Channels, Connect, Move Members and Manage Channels, and never Manage Roles. Existing installations may need the bot invited again to grant them.
strings.web.proximity.createHelp: BedrockRelay can create a dedicated category and silent opt-in lobby with the right permissions.
strings.web.proximity.createdText: The category and lobby were created and proximity voice is enabled for {server}.
strings.web.proximity.enabledText: Proximity voice is now enabled for {server}.
strings.web.proximity.disabledText: Proximity voice is now disabled for {server}.
strings.web.language.title: Language in Discord
strings.web.language.intro: What BedrockRelay writes in this Discord server: joins, leaves and deaths, connection notices, and its answers to commands. Chat is never translated.
strings.web.language.label: Language
strings.web.language.help: Automatic follows the language in this Discord server's Community settings. Missing a language, or found a mistake? {link}
strings.web.channels.noneUsable: BedrockRelay can't use any channel here yet
strings.web.channels.permissionHelp: Their permission settings stop BedrockRelay from seeing them or posting in them. Give the BedrockRelay role View Channel and Manage Webhooks in the channel's settings, then check again.
strings.web.events.hint: Tick none for a channel that gets only the plugin posts you choose for it, like a staff channel for alerts.
strings.web.routes.title: Channel routes
strings.web.routes.none: No channels connected yet. Add one below to start relaying.
strings.web.routes.channelGone: This channel no longer exists. Remove the route, or connect another channel.
strings.web.routes.lostPermissions: BedrockRelay has lost {permissions} in this channel, so messages to and from it will fail.
strings.web.routes.disconnectText: Messages stop relaying to and from this channel. You can connect it again below.
strings.web.routes.notYours: Owned by someone else. Only its owner can change this route.
strings.web.routes.savedPluginsOnly: {channel} now gets only the plugin posts you choose for it.
strings.web.routes.connectedHint: Edit each channel's direction, events and shared chat, then save its changes.
strings.web.routes.addHint: Connect another Discord channel to a Minecraft server.
strings.web.routes.addFirst: Set up a Minecraft server of your own and give the bot access to a text channel first.
strings.web.sftp.folderLong: Minecraft server folder (the one with server.properties and worlds/)
strings.web.sftp.keyPlaceholder: Optional: an SSH private key instead of a password
strings.web.sftp.remember: Remember these details on this device. Never the password or key.
strings.web.sftp.missingText: Enter the SFTP host, username, and password or private key.
strings.web.preview.stopped: My Minecraft server is stopped right now.
strings.web.mc.notConnected: Not connected to a channel yet
strings.web.mc.sparklineLabel: Messages per day for the last 7 days: {values}
strings.web.mc.removedUndo: You can undo this for 7 days under Recently removed.
strings.web.chart.title: Last 30 days
strings.web.chart.empty: Nothing recorded yet. Statistics start from the first message relayed after this dashboard was updated.
strings.web.chart.label: Messages relayed per day for the last 30 days, by direction. A table view follows.
strings.web.removed.title: Recently removed
strings.web.removed.intro: These Minecraft servers are disconnected. Undo brings back their channels, statistics and pack connection exactly as they were.
strings.web.removed.backText: Its channels and statistics are exactly as they were. Its pack reconnects on its next check-in.
strings.web.removed.deleteText: Its statistics and the bot's webhooks in its channels are deleted now, and it can't be undone.
strings.web.removed.deletedText: Its statistics and webhooks are gone.
strings.web.connections.title: Discord channels
strings.web.connections.none: This Minecraft server is not connected to any channel yet.
strings.web.commands.title: Commands from Discord
strings.web.commands.intro: People can run Minecraft commands with /relay run in a connected channel, but only the commands you allow here. Discord administrators can run any allowed command; a role widens that to its members.
strings.web.commands.connectFirst: Connect this Minecraft server to a channel first — commands are run from connected channels.
strings.web.commands.roleGone: A role that no longer exists
strings.web.commands.none: No commands are allowed yet, so /relay run refuses everything.
strings.web.commands.starWarning: * allows every command, including op, deop and stop. Only use it with a role you trust completely.
strings.web.commands.enterText: Type the command you want to allow, like weather.
strings.web.serverPlugins.intro: Plugins add Discord commands for your Minecraft world. Installed plugins appear here after the Minecraft server restarts; switch one on to add its commands to the Discord servers this Minecraft server is connected to. Answers are only shown to the person who asked, unless the plugin says they're for everyone. Plugins that post by themselves only post in the channels you choose.
strings.web.serverPlugins.connectForRoles: Connect a channel to add roles.
strings.web.serverPlugins.kindsNeedPack: Until the pack is updated to v{version}, it posts all of these.
strings.web.serverPlugins.needPack: Plugins need pack v{version} or newer
strings.web.serverPlugins.hasPack: {server} has v{version}. Update the pack, restart the Minecraft server, and its plugins will appear here.
strings.web.serverPlugins.updatesText: Updates install over SFTP like the plugins did, then take effect when the Minecraft server restarts. Your switches, roles and channels stay as they are.
strings.web.serverPlugins.none: No plugins are installed on this Minecraft server yet.
strings.web.links.title: Linked accounts
strings.web.links.intro: Members link their Discord account to their Minecraft player with {command} in a connected channel. We whisper a code to that player in game, so nobody can claim someone else. Linked members can use plugins like /lastdeath without typing a name.
strings.web.links.none: Nobody has linked their account yet.
strings.web.security.title: Security
strings.web.security.intro: Your pack proves who it is with a token that's built in when it's installed. If the pack zip or its config files may have leaked, revoke every token; reinstalling issues a new one.
strings.web.security.warning: The pack on {server} stops connecting straight away and stays quiet until you reinstall it. Use this if your pack zip or config files may have been seen by someone else.
strings.web.security.revokedText: The pack on {server} can't connect until you reinstall it, which issues a new token.
strings.web.join.title: Where players join
strings.web.join.label: Join address
strings.web.join.whileRunning: Checked while the Minecraft server is running.
strings.web.join.okAnswers: Players can join at {address} — it answers as “{name}”.
strings.web.join.blankText: It answers at {address}, but with no server details, so Minecraft treats it as offline. Turn on {setting} in server.properties or your host's panel, then restart.
strings.web.join.silentText: Nothing answered at {address}. Check the port is open to players, or if players use a different address, enter it below.
strings.web.join.unresolvedText: {address} doesn't resolve to a server. Check it for typos.
strings.web.join.private: It connects from a private address ({address}), so we can't check it from the internet. If players join from outside your network, enter the address they use below.
strings.web.join.automaticText: {server} is checked at the address it connects from again.
strings.web.join.hintSet: BedrockRelay checks this address about once a minute while the server is running.
strings.web.join.hintAutomatic: Leave empty to check the address your Minecraft server connects from, on the port in server.properties. Enter the address players use if that's different, e.g. play.example.com:19132.
strings.web.uninstall.title: Remove {server}?
strings.web.uninstall.intro: It is disconnected from every Discord channel straight away, and its pack is no longer accepted. You can undo this from your dashboard for 7 days; after that it is gone for good.
strings.web.uninstall.justRemoveText: The pack stays on your Minecraft server but can no longer connect. You can uninstall it yourself whenever you like.
strings.web.uninstall.alsoUninstall: Also uninstall the pack over SFTP
strings.web.uninstall.alsoUninstallText: We connect once, show exactly what will change, and remove only what BedrockRelay added.
strings.web.uninstall.nothingText: No BedrockRelay files were found in that folder. Removing will only disconnect it from BedrockRelay.
strings.web.uninstall.betaText: Turn it off only if nothing else on the world needs it. Achievements stay disabled for the world either way — Bedrock never re-enables them once an experiment has been used.
strings.web.uninstall.manualWorld: In {file}, delete the entry whose pack_id is {id}. Keep every other entry.
strings.web.uninstall.manualConfig: In {variables} delete the keys starting with {prefix}, and in {secrets} delete {token}. If there is a {folder} folder, delete it.
strings.web.uninstall.manualBeta: Optionally turn Beta APIs off in your world settings, if no other pack needs it. Achievements stay disabled for that world either way.
strings.web.setup.subtitle: From Discord invite to pack installation, all in one place.
strings.web.setup.step1: Add the bot to a Discord server
strings.web.setup.updateText: Install the new pack over the old one, then restart your Minecraft server. Your channels and settings stay as they are.
strings.web.setup.newTitle: Let's get your Minecraft server talking to Discord.
strings.web.setup.newText: Five short steps, one at a time. Everything happens here in your dashboard.
strings.web.setup.guildNeededText: Create a Discord server, or ask for Manage Server permission in one, before setting up BedrockRelay.
strings.web.setup.inviteWaiting: Discord says BedrockRelay was added. Waiting for it to arrive in {guild}…
strings.web.setup.inviteCancelled: The bot was not added. You can try again whenever you're ready.
strings.web.setup.inviteNeeded: BedrockRelay needs to join {guild}. You'll approve it on Discord and come straight back here.
strings.web.setup.nameNeededText: Give your Minecraft server a name, like the one players know it by.
strings.web.setup.nameText: This is how it will be labelled in Discord and in your dashboard. Your world's name works well.
strings.web.setup.existing: Or show a Minecraft server you've already connected to another Discord server:
strings.web.setup.advancedHint: Leave these alone unless your host tells you otherwise.
strings.web.setup.moduleConfig: Use a per-module config folder instead of config/default (VPS or self-hosted Minecraft servers only)
strings.web.setup.stopFirst: Stop your Minecraft server first, then choose how to install.
strings.web.setup.waitingVersion: Waiting for {server} to connect with pack v{version}…
strings.web.setup.waitingText: Start (or restart) your Minecraft server. This page moves on by itself the moment the pack checks in.
strings.web.setup.trouble1: Beta APIs must be on for the world. Without it the pack loads but stays silent.
strings.web.setup.trouble2: Your console should show a line starting [BedrockRelay] connected to. No [BedrockRelay] line at all means the pack did not load.
strings.web.setup.trouble3: Make sure the server is running the world the pack was installed to.
strings.web.setup.skipChoose: Skip for now and choose a channel
strings.web.setup.notConnectedYet: Not connected yet. It starts relaying as soon as it does.
strings.web.setup.runningPack: {server} is running pack v{version}. Its channels and settings are just as they were.
strings.web.setup.nextStart: The new pack takes over the next time {server} starts. Its channels and settings are just as they were.
strings.web.setup.relayingTo: {server} is relaying to {channels}. Say something in Minecraft to see it arrive.
strings.web.setup.channelText: Minecraft chat, joins, leaves and deaths will appear in this channel, and messages sent there will appear in Minecraft. You can add more channels and filters afterwards.
strings.web.setup.noChannels: This Discord server has no text channels yet. Create one, then refresh.
strings.web.install.addedTo: BedrockRelay will be added to {world}, alongside any packs already there.
strings.web.install.backedUp: Every existing file we change is backed up first, next to the original.
strings.web.install.betaOn: Beta APIs will be turned on. Achievements are disabled for this world from now on.
strings.web.install.liability: I understand BedrockRelay has checked everything it can, but my Minecraft server and its backups are my responsibility, and BedrockRelay is not liable for any loss or damage. See the {terms}.
strings.web.install.betaTitle: Beta APIs must be on for this world
strings.web.install.betaText: BedrockRelay reads chat through a Minecraft feature that is still experimental, so it cannot work without Beta APIs. Turning on any experiment permanently disables achievements for this world.
strings.web.install.betaAccept: Turn on Beta APIs for this world. I understand achievements will be disabled for it permanently.
strings.web.install.connecting: Connecting to your Minecraft server and preparing a preview…
strings.web.install.notBds: This folder does not look like a Bedrock server.
strings.web.install.noWorlds: No worlds were found. Start your Minecraft server once to create one.
strings.web.install.sftpIntro: Your SFTP details are in your host's control panel. We connect once, show every planned change before writing anything, and never store them.
strings.web.download.doneText: Follow the installation steps below it to put it on your Minecraft server.
strings.web.download.intro: Download a pack with your Minecraft server's settings already filled in. Keep the zip private because it contains your installation token.
strings.web.download.step2: Unzip into the folder with server.properties and worlds/. Merge files rather than replacing other packs.
strings.web.download.step3: Add the BedrockRelay entry from INSTALL.txt to your world's world_behavior_packs.json, keeping existing entries.
strings.web.download.step4: Turn on Beta APIs for the world. It is required, and like any experiment it permanently disables achievements for that world.
strings.web.catalog.title: Add commands to your Minecraft servers
strings.web.catalog.intro: Every plugin here has been reviewed. Add the ones you want to your list, then apply them in one go — one connection per Minecraft server. Restart the server, then switch each plugin on from that server's page. Every plugin's code is {github}, where you can also submit your own. Building one? {guide}.
strings.web.catalog.setUpFirst: Set up a Minecraft server first
strings.web.catalog.setUpFirstText: Plugins are installed onto a Minecraft server that's running BedrockRelay.
strings.web.catalog.empty: There are no plugins in the catalog yet.
strings.web.catalog.restartSwitch: Restart {server}, then switch the new plugins on from its page.

web.catalog.manualFolder.one: Put it in {folder} on your Minecraft server.
web.catalog.manualFolder.other: Put them in {folder} on your Minecraft server.

strings.web.catalog.manualIndex: In {file}, add {names} to the list, e.g. {example}.
strings.web.catalog.manualRestart: Restart the Minecraft server, then switch each plugin on from its page.
strings.web.catalog.restartText: Plugins load when a Minecraft server starts, so these changes take effect the next time you restart {server}. It can keep running while we copy the files.
strings.web.catalog.restartSwitchOn: After the restart, switch the new plugins on from its page.
strings.web.catalog.touchOnly: We touch only these plugins' files and their lines in the plugin list, exactly as reviewed, over one connection. Your SFTP details are used once and never stored.
strings.web.catalog.touchOnlyOwn: We touch only these plugins' files and their lines in the plugin list, over one connection. Your own plugins are installed exactly as you uploaded them. Your SFTP details are used once and never stored.
strings.web.catalog.own.onlyYou: Your own plugin · only you can see it
strings.web.catalog.own.title: Your own plugins
strings.web.catalog.own.intro: Upload a plugin you've written for your own Minecraft servers. It isn't reviewed, and it's listed only here, on your dashboard. It installs like any other plugin.
strings.web.catalog.own.uploadHelp: Choose the plugin's .js file. We read its {id}, name, {version} and description, and check its format. Uploading a file with the same id again replaces it. {guide}.
strings.web.catalog.own.newVersionHelp: Choose the updated .js file, with a higher {version}, so your Minecraft servers are offered the update. {guide}.
strings.web.catalog.own.notReviewedText: It runs on your Minecraft server with the full Minecraft Script API, so only upload code you wrote or trust. The BedrockRelay team can see what's uploaded and where it's used.
strings.web.catalog.own.addedText: Add it to your list below to install it on your Minecraft servers.
strings.web.catalog.own.updatedText: Version {version} is ready. Add the update to your list to install it.
strings.web.catalog.own.differentId: That file's id is {id}, not {was}, so it was added as a separate plugin.
strings.web.catalog.own.deleteText: It's removed from your dashboard. You can upload it again at any time.
